verdicts.factCheck: I fetched the cited client sources. bnb-chain/bsc v1.8.2 params/protocol_params.go line 31 sets MaxTxGas to 1 << 24 and keeps ColdSloadCostEIP2929 2100 (line 72) and SstoreResetGasEIP2200 5000 (line 68). 0xPolygon/bor v2.11.1 params/protocol_params.go line 32 sets MaxTxGas to 1 << 25, and lines 76 and 77 set ColdSloadCostPIP88 5460 and ColdSstoreCostPIP88 2940. core/vm/operations_acl.go line 152 charges SstoreResetGasEIP2200 minus ColdSstoreCostPIP88 for a write to an existing slot. ava-labs/avalanchego v1.15.3 vms/saevm/worstcase/state.go refuses an operation only when its gas exceeds what is left of the block (Apply, lines 295 to 297) and sets the block limit from the gas rate (lines 123 and 146 to 153). On chain on 2026-11-24: eth_estimateGas of an endless loop (0x5b600056) returned gas required exceeds allowance (16777216) on bsc-dataseed1 (web3_clientVersion Geth/v1.8.2), (33554432) on polygon.drpc.org, and (50000000) on api.avax.network (avalanchego/1.15.3). The Avalanche figure is the RPC allowance of the endpoint, not a consensus cap, which fits the finding. eth_gasPrice returned 0x2faf080 (0.05 gwei), 0x4133f72d7f (about 280 gwei) and 0x1c2a6a802 (about 7.56 gwei). An eth_call that runs CLZ returned 0xff on BSC and Polygon and invalid opcode 0x1e on Avalanche. eth_call did not enforce the 2^24 cap at gas 0x4000000 on BSC, so the cap applies to transactions and estimateGas, not to eth_call. The per crossing gas figures are computed and not measured, as the finding says; the repository snapshots hold no tick crossing figure.
verdicts.codeCheck: The swap loop runs one step per initialized tick or per bitmap word (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344, nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord at src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:85-119). A step that lands on an initialized tick calls crossTick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:420), which reads and writes feeGrowthOutside0X128 and feeGrowthOutside1X128 and reads liquidityNet (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-611): three cold reads and two writes, 12,100 gas under Ethereum prices, which matches the finding. The loop ends at sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a swap can be split into valid pieces. modifyLiquidity has no loop and updates two ticks, at most two bitmap words and one position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236), so removal gas does not depend on the number of ticks. 1.0001^1000 is 1.105 and MIN_TICK/256 is 3,466 words, both as stated.
verdicts.corrections: The hazard is the same on Ethereum, which has the same 2^24 cap; only the native cost of building the tick run differs, so the network difference is one of price, not of rule. The Avalanche claim that the C-Chain charges at least half of the gas limit is not supported by the lines cited and was not checked. Whether the saevm code path is the one live on C-Chain mainnet was not confirmed; the client version on the endpoint is avalanchego 1.15.3.

sources.supports: Only the remaining block gas bounds a transaction (lines 295 to 297); accept mask of tx types 0, 1, 2 (lines 181 to 193).

verdicts.factCheck: I read the receipt and the call trace of the first payout 0x63916a377cf61da0672647f44a612d9dffc080972ada0371a71689125e0ec2f4 (block 106,450,859, status 1, sent by 0x2d68a551e7c8ecf7312ee083a16e736dce2347d5 to 0x3c69c0620ca6bd0df44c0aa8c39602f7c3ebdf27). debug_traceTransaction with callTracer at the NodeReal endpoint shows, inside the PoolManager unlock (0x48c89491) and its callback: sync (0xa5841194) with balanceOf returning 0x1479bbba235, the rebase call 0xaf14052c on the staking contract 0x6bcd1273eba684ff62614e41eff87123113112d1, settle (0x11da60b4) returning 0x8245fc9 (136,601,545) after balanceOf returned 0x147a3e001fe, and take (0x0b0d9c09) transferring sNVB out. The receipt holds the two rebase logs of sNVB, a transfer of 136,601,545 from the PoolManager to 0x3c69c062, no PoolManager event, and a sale of the same amount through pair 0x2df8dd88da7fae1fbc995cdcd43517544b245fb3 for 0x1bc1e76aae7528f base units of BSC-USD 0x55d398326f99059ff775485246999027b3197955 (0.12501 USD) paid to the sender. Archive eth_call at bsc.api.pocket.network and at NodeReal both give balanceOf(PoolManager) 1,407,067,071,029 at blocks 106,450,858 and 106,450,859 and index() 46,185,701,171 then 46,190,184,993, as the finding states. I did not recount the 469 transactions or the total of 94.0989 sNVB.
verdicts.codeCheck: sync stores balanceOf(PoolManager) (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). _settle credits reservesNow minus reservesBefore for the synced currency with msg.value zero (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). take debits the caller and transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). The deltas close to zero, so the check at src/PoolManager.sol:112 passes. The rise from a public rebase between sync and settle is credited to the caller, which is the traced sequence.
verdicts.corrections: The amounts are not unpriced: the traced payout sold 136,601,545 base units of sNVB for 0.12501 BSC-USD in the same transaction through pair 0x2df8dd88da7fae1fbc995cdcd43517544b245fb3, so the total is of the order of 100 USD. Actor unprivileged stands because the token is not attacker-made and the rebase is public, but the amounts back no position (F-070), so no user balance fell; this is a token hazard outside the opcode focus of this cycle and should stay a one-line record.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Exits: can an ordinary account make another user's liquidity removal or claim redemption impossible to include on these networks through gas caps, storage prices or the cost of tick crossings.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Pool.modifyLiquidity has no loop and touches two ticks, at most two bitmap words via flipTick, getFeeGrowthInside of two ticks and one position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236). TickLiquidityOverflow applies only when liquidityDelta is not negative (src/libraries/Pool.sol:164-172), so it cannot block a removal. burn and take have no loop (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 332-336). The caps of 2^24 and 2^25 were confirmed by eth_estimateGas on bsc-dataseed1 and polygon.drpc.org, far above the cost of one removal.

clearedSpotChecks.check: The fork boundary of Jenner on 2026-12-08. Until then a transfer call to 0x70 or to a CAS20 address succeeds with empty data. Can an account create a debt, a credit, a claim or pool liquidity in such a currency before the fork that becomes a claim on real tokens after it.
clearedSpotChecks.note: The build uses solc 0.8.26 (foundry.toml line 6). balanceOfSelf is a high level call that decodes a uint256 (src/types/Currency.sol:88-94), so an empty answer from an address without code makes sync revert and no credit can be made. take succeeds on empty return data (src/types/Currency.sol:64-72) but only adds a debt (src/PoolManager.sol:294). mint adds a debt equal to the claim (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329) and burn needs claims. With no source of credit, no unlock that touched such a currency can close (src/PoolManager.sol:112). After the fork a precompile at 0x70 answering 32 bytes makes balanceOf return a value that is constant within the transaction, so settle credits zero. I did not query 0x70 myself.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Exits: special recipients. Can an outsider make the native payout of another user's take revert, or does any of the three chains refuse value transfers from the PoolManager to particular recipients.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched bsc v1.8.2 core/vm/evm.go. Call skips the balance check and the value transfer only when isSystemCall(caller) is true, which compares the caller with params.SystemAddress (lines 291 to 293, 314 and 343 to 347). The PoolManager is never that address. The native branch of transfer forwards all gas to a recipient the caller chose (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52).

leads.question: Is the vms/saevm execution path of avalanchego 1.15.3 the one that decides C-Chain mainnet blocks today, or does the C-Chain still run the earlier coreth path, and do the cleared items of this unit on transaction types and on worst case inclusion hold for the path that is live?
leads.why: Three cleared items and the Avalanche part of the gas finding rest on saevm source. The endpoint reports avalanchego/1.15.3, which does not by itself show which VM serves the C-Chain.
